_about: Book of the day. One book a day, in this order, looping. Add a book anywhere in the list (keep the same fields). t/a = English title/author, tz/az = Chinese title/author (leave out if unsure), tag = 科技/AI/科學/歷史/小說/商業/心理/生活, en/zh = short brief, ken/kzh = one idea to keep. Covers are saved as books/<id>.jpg by .github/workflows/books.yml (optional isbn picks the edition; cover set to an empty string means draw a plain cover; delete a wrong books/<id>.jpg to fetch it again).

books.en: How the tiny silicon chip became the world's most fought-over resource. Miller follows the story from the first transistors in California to Taiwan's TSMC, and shows why whoever makes the most advanced chips holds real power over phones, cars and weapons.
books.zh: 一粒小小的晶片，點樣變成全世界爭奪最激烈的資源？作者由加州第一批電晶體講起，一路講到台積電，解釋點解邊個掌握最先進的晶片，就等於掌握手機、汽車以至武器的命脈。
books.ken: Almost every advanced chip passes through a handful of companies, which makes them a point of global tension.
books.kzh: 全球最先進的晶片只靠幾間公司生產，所以佢哋成為大國角力的焦點。

books.en: A sweeping history of humankind in one book: how a modest ape conquered the planet. Harari argues our superpower is believing in shared stories, such as money, nations and companies, which lets millions of strangers work together.
books.zh: 用一本書講完人類嘅歷史：一種普通嘅猿類點樣征服地球。作者認為人類最大嘅本領，係相信大家共同嘅「故事」，例如金錢、國家同公司，令素未謀面嘅人都可以一齊合作。
books.ken: Money, laws and countries work because we all agree to believe in them.
books.kzh: 金錢、法律同國家之所以行得通，係因為大家都願意相信佢哋。

books.en: The story of the digital revolution, from Ada Lovelace's 1840s notes on a mechanical computer to Google. Isaacson shows that the computer, the chip and the internet were built by teams that mixed science, engineering and art, not by lone geniuses.
books.zh: 數碼革命嘅故事：由 1840 年代 Ada Lovelace 寫低嘅第一個電腦程式構想，到 Google 誕生。作者指出電腦、晶片同互聯網都係團隊合作嘅成果，結合科學、工程同藝術，而唔係單靠一個天才。
books.ken: Big inventions come from teams that mix different kinds of people.
books.kzh: 偉大嘅發明，多數來自由唔同背景嘅人組成嘅團隊。

books.en: A science teacher wakes up alone on a spaceship light-years from Earth with no memory of how he got there. He must use real science and plenty of humour to save humanity, and makes a very unexpected friend along the way.
books.zh: 一個中學科學老師喺太空船上醒來，身處離地球幾光年嘅地方，完全唔記得自己點解會喺度。佢要靠真實嘅科學知識同幽默感拯救人類，仲喺途中結識咗一位意想不到嘅朋友。
books.ken: Science is just careful problem solving, one step at a time.
books.kzh: 科學其實就係一步一步、小心咁解決問題。

books.en: In a near-future Britain where a long crisis has left government weak and the sea full of strange new creatures, Phillip Tennent scrapes a living collecting things that wash up from the Channel. One day he pulls out a shape-shifting object he cannot keep, and has to carry it inland. Harrison, a veteran of science fiction, is the first SF writer to win the Booker.
books.more_en: It reads as a quiet, eerie road novel more than an action story: the comedy and sadness of a country running down, gentrified seaside towns, and ordinary people adapting to a world that no longer works. Short at 224 pages, with spare, unsentimental sentences. Good for readers who liked the mood of Station Eleven or Annihilation but want something stranger and more British.
books.zh: 近未來嘅英國，長期危機令政府無力，海入面仲出現咗啲古怪新生物。Phillip Tennent 靠喺英倫海峽執海上漂來嘅物件維生。有一日佢撈起一件會變形嘅神秘物體，留唔住又掟唔走，唯有帶住佢一路向內陸行。作者係資深科幻作家，係第一位攞布克獎嘅科幻小說家。
books.more_zh: 呢本書唔係動作片式嘅末日小說，而係一段靜靜哋、有啲詭異嘅旅程：一個國家慢慢失靈，海邊小鎮被「士紳化」，普通人點樣喺壞咗嘅世界度繼續過日子。全書只有 224 頁，文字簡潔冷靜，帶黑色幽默。

reviews.d: Strange and unsettling; admires Harrison's spare, unsentimental prose.
reviews.dz: 奇特又令人不安；文字簡潔冷靜，唔煽情。

reviews.d: A sharp picture of collapse and a lament for post-Brexit Britain, with satire of trendy coastal towns. You may argue with it but will enjoy it.
reviews.dz: 環境崩壞同脫歐後英國嘅輓歌，諷刺海邊潮流小鎮；未必全部認同，但會睇得過癮。

books.ken: The end of the world may not be a bang, just everything slowly ceasing to work.
books.kzh: 世界末日未必係一聲巨響，可能只係所有嘢慢慢唔再運作。

books.en: How do computers actually work? Starting with flashlights and Morse code, Petzold builds up, step by step, to relays, logic gates, memory and a working computer. A rare book that makes the inside of a computer feel simple.
books.zh: 電腦究竟點樣運作？作者由手電筒同摩斯密碼開始，一步一步砌出繼電器、邏輯閘、記憶體，最後變成一部真正嘅電腦。少有一本書可以令電腦內部變得咁易明。
books.ken: Every computer is built from very simple on/off switches.
books.kzh: 再複雜嘅電腦，都係由最簡單嘅「開關」砌出嚟。

books.en: A practical guide to building good habits and breaking bad ones. Clear shows how tiny 1% changes add up, and gives four simple rules: make it obvious, attractive, easy and satisfying.
books.zh: 一本教你建立好習慣、戒除壞習慣嘅實用書。作者講解每日進步 1% 點樣累積成巨大改變，並提出四個簡單法則：令佢明顯、吸引、容易同有滿足感。
books.ken: You do not rise to your goals; you fall to the level of your systems.
books.kzh: 決定你成就嘅唔係目標，而係你每日嘅習慣系統。

books.en: Taiwan, 1938, under Japanese rule. A popular Japanese novelist, Aoyama Chizuko, arrives for a lecture tour and is given a Taiwanese interpreter, Ō Chizuru. As they travel the island and eat their way through it, a close friendship grows, but one shaped by who rules and who serves. The first Taiwanese book to win the International Booker.
books.more_en: The novel is cleverly dressed as a real rediscovered travel memoir, complete with translator's notes and afterwords, so the question of who gets to tell Taiwan's story runs right through it. Food is everywhere: rice noodles, melon, sweet soups, banquets. A gentle, bittersweet read about affection, power and colonial history, especially rich for anyone who knows Taiwan or Hong Kong.
books.zh: 1938 年，日治時期嘅台灣。日本人氣女作家青山千鶴子嚟台灣巡迴演講，獲安排一位台灣通譯王千鶴陪同。兩人一齊環島、一路食盡台灣美食，感情愈來愈深，但呢段友誼始終隔住統治者同被統治者嘅身份。係第一本贏得國際布克獎嘅台灣作品。
books.more_zh: 小說巧妙咁扮成一本重新出土嘅旅行回憶錄，連譯者註同後記都有，令「邊個有權講台灣故事」呢個問題貫穿全書。書入面處處都係食物：米粉、甜湯、筵席。溫柔又帶苦澀，講感情、權力同殖民歷史；對熟悉台灣同香港嘅讀者特別有共鳴。

reviews.d: Praises its layered colonial politics; the ambiguity of the central relationship is what gives the novel its power.
reviews.dz: 殖民政治層次豐富；兩位主角關係嘅曖昧正正係本書力量所在。

reviews.q: The food-talk can be a bit much
reviews.d: Clever and colourful, strong on translation and empire, though the food writing gets heavy. Grade B.
reviews.dz: 聰明又多姿多彩，翻譯同帝國嘅主題處理得好；不過食物描寫有啲多。評級 B。

books.ken: Even a warm friendship can't escape the power gap between the people in it.
books.kzh: 再真摯嘅友誼，都逃唔出兩個人之間嘅權力差距。

books.en: The authorised biography of Apple's co-founder, based on over forty interviews with Jobs himself. It covers the garage start, being fired from his own company, the comeback with the iMac, iPod and iPhone, and his demanding, brilliant personality.
books.zh: 蘋果創辦人喬布斯嘅官方傳記，作者同佢本人做咗四十幾次訪問。由車房創業、被自己公司炒魷魚，到憑 iMac、iPod 同 iPhone 捲土重來，以及佢要求極高又才華橫溢嘅性格，都寫得好清楚。
books.ken: Great products come from caring about details nobody else will see.
books.kzh: 好產品來自連無人會留意嘅細節都用心做好。

books.en: During China's Cultural Revolution, a secret project sends a signal into space, and an alien civilisation answers. Decades later, scientists start dying mysteriously. A mind-bending science fiction story about physics, history and first contact.
books.zh: 文革期間，一個秘密項目向太空發出訊號，竟然收到外星文明回覆。幾十年後，科學家接連離奇死亡。一個結合物理、歷史同外星接觸嘅科幻故事，令人腦洞大開。
books.ken: Making contact with aliens might be the most dangerous thing we could do.
books.kzh: 同外星文明接觸，可能係人類做得出最危險嘅事。

books.en: Sybil Van Antwerp is a 73-year-old retired lawyer who still writes letters every day: to her brother, her children, old friends, even authors whose books she loved or loathed. Told entirely through her letters over nine years, the novel slowly reveals a painful past, grief for a son, failing eyesight, and one letter she has never been able to send. A debut novel.
books.more_en: It is funny as well as sad: Sybil is sharp, opinionated and sometimes impossible, and her complaints to strangers are a joy. Because it is all letters, the book reads quickly and is easy to dip into, and it builds to a moving close about forgiveness and late-life friendship. A word-of-mouth bestseller and a favourite of book clubs.
books.zh: Sybil Van Antwerp 係一位 73 歲嘅退休律師，每日都仲寫信：寫畀弟弟、仔女、老朋友，甚至寫畀佢鍾意或者憎嘅作家。全書由佢九年間嘅書信組成，慢慢揭開佢痛苦嘅過去、對兒子嘅哀傷、日漸衰退嘅視力，同埋一封佢一直寄唔出嘅信。作者嘅第一本小說。
books.more_zh: 呢本書又好笑又好感人：Sybil 牙尖嘴利、好有主見，有時仲好難頂，佢寫信畀陌生人投訴嗰啲段落好過癮。因為全部係書信，好易入口、可以一段一段咁睇，結尾講寬恕同晚年友情，好打動人。口碑相傳嘅暢銷書，讀書會最愛。

reviews.q: does not put a foot wrong
reviews.d: A confident debut that balances sorrow and humour with great skill; readers will fall for Sybil.
reviews.dz: 自信嘅處女作，悲傷同幽默拿捏得好準；讀者會愛上 Sybil。

reviews.d: Emotionally resonant, with a voice that lingers long after; ideal for book clubs.
reviews.dz: 情感深刻，主角把聲睇完仲喺腦海；好適合讀書會。

books.ken: It is never too late to say what you meant, even in a letter you nearly didn't send.
books.kzh: 想講嘅說話永遠唔會太遲，就算係一封差啲寄唔出嘅信。

books.en: What happens if we build a machine smarter than us? Philosopher Nick Bostrom explores the paths to superintelligent AI and why controlling it could be humanity's hardest problem. The book that started today's AI safety debate.
books.zh: 如果人類造出比自己更聰明嘅機器，會點？哲學家博斯特倫探討超級人工智能可能點樣出現，以及點解控制佢可能係人類最難嘅問題。呢本書開啟咗今日關於 AI 安全嘅討論。
books.ken: A very smart system with the wrong goal is dangerous, even without bad intent.
books.kzh: 一個好聰明但目標唔啱嘅系統，就算冇惡意都可以好危險。

books.en: Stephen Hawking explains the biggest questions in physics, such as the Big Bang, black holes and the nature of time, for ordinary readers, with almost no equations. One of the best-selling science books ever written.
books.zh: 霍金用淺白嘅文字，幾乎冇方程式，向普通讀者解釋物理學最大嘅問題：大爆炸、黑洞同時間嘅本質。史上最暢銷嘅科普書之一。
books.ken: Time had a beginning, and black holes are not completely black.
books.kzh: 時間有起點，而黑洞其實並唔係完全黑。

books.en: France, the last weeks of the First World War. Cyril Bagger, an American private and card cheat, and four other soldiers are sent into no man's land to find the source of an unearthly shriek. What they find is an angel, tangled in barbed wire. Now they must decide what to do with her, and what she means. The whole novel is written as one long sentence.
books.more_en: That single breathless sentence sounds like a gimmick but works: it pulls you through the mud, gas and terror at the soldiers' pace. It is grisly and cinematic, yet also strangely beautiful and full of questions about faith, cowardice and mercy. Kraus is known for horror and co-wrote The Shape of Water with Guillermo del Toro.
books.zh: 第一次世界大戰最後幾個星期嘅法國戰場。美國二等兵兼出千高手 Cyril Bagger 同四個戰友，奉命走入無人地帶，搵出一陣非人尖叫聲嘅來源。佢哋發現嘅，竟然係一個纏喺鐵絲網上嘅天使。佢哋要決定點樣處置佢，同埋佢代表咩。全本小說只係一句長句。
books.more_zh: 成本書一句到底，聽落似噱頭，但其實好有效：拖住你喺泥漿、毒氣同恐懼之中，跟住士兵嘅節奏前進。畫面血腥、好有電影感，但又出奇地美，探討信仰、懦弱同憐憫。作者以恐怖小說見稱，曾同 Guillermo del Toro 合寫《忘形水》。

reviews.q: breathes new life into the war novel
reviews.d: Vivid and relentlessly paced, with lyrical flights; it refreshes the war-novel form.
reviews.dz: 畫面鮮明、節奏緊湊，間中好有詩意；為戰爭小說注入新生命。

reviews.q: strangely gorgeous amid its visceral ugliness
reviews.d: The one-sentence style seems a gimmick at first but proves necessary; grisly and cinematic yet beautiful.
reviews.dz: 一句到底初時似噱頭，後來覺得必要；血腥又有電影感，但好美。

books.ken: In the middle of horror, people still have to choose what kind of person to be.
books.kzh: 就算身處地獄，人仍然要揀自己做一個點樣嘅人。

books.t: The Soul of a New Machine
books.en: A Pulitzer Prize-winning look inside a team of young engineers racing to build a new computer in 18 months. It captures the long nights, the pressure and the joy of making something new, and still feels true for tech teams today.
books.zh: 普立茲獎作品，記錄一班年輕工程師喺 18 個月內趕製一部新電腦嘅經過。通宵開工、巨大壓力，同創造新事物嘅喜悅都寫得好真實，今日嘅科技團隊讀落一樣有共鳴。
books.ken: People will work incredibly hard for the chance to build something they believe in.
books.kzh: 為咗有機會做自己相信嘅嘢，人可以付出驚人嘅努力。

books.en: Nobel prize winner Daniel Kahneman explains the two systems in our heads: a fast, intuitive one and a slow, careful one. He shows the many ways quick thinking fools us, from money decisions to judging other people.
books.zh: 諾貝爾獎得主康納曼解釋我哋腦入面嘅兩個系統：一個快速、靠直覺；一個緩慢、謹慎。佢列舉咗好多例子，話你知快思考點樣喺理財同判斷他人時誤導我哋。
books.ken: When a decision matters, slow down: your first instinct is often biased.
books.kzh: 重要嘅決定要慢慢諗，因為第一直覺往往有偏差。

books.en: István is fifteen, living with his mother on a Hungarian housing estate, when he begins a secret relationship with a married neighbour that goes terribly wrong. The novel follows him through the army, war and then London's world of the very rich, as his search for love, status and money brings him wealth that threatens to undo him. A whole life told in short, spare scenes.
books.more_en: Szalay leaves a lot unsaid: István rarely explains himself, and much happens in the gaps between chapters, so the reader fills in the feelings. The Booker judges praised its cool detachment and its pace; some readers find it bleak. Quick to read despite its length, and a sharp look at men, class and how little control we have over our lives.
books.zh: István 十五歲，同媽媽住喺匈牙利一個屋邨，同一位已婚女鄰居開始咗一段秘密關係，結果出咗大事。小說跟住佢入軍隊、上戰場，再去到倫敦富豪圈子；佢追求愛、地位同金錢，換嚟嘅財富卻差啲毀咗佢。用一幕幕簡短冷靜嘅場景，寫完一個男人嘅一生。
books.more_zh: 作者留白好多：István 好少解釋自己，好多事都發生喺章與章之間，要讀者自己補返感受。布克獎評審讚佢冷靜抽離、節奏明快；亦有讀者覺得太灰。篇幅唔短但好快睇完，深刻咁寫男人、階級，同人對自己命運幾咁身不由己。

reviews.d: A moving portrait of a quiet, closed-off man, as quoted in PW's report of the win.
reviews.dz: 一個沉默寡言男人嘅動人寫照（PW 報道得獎時引述）。

reviews.d: Admires the pared-down style but finds the tone pessimistic and the ending bleak; a dissenting view.
reviews.dz: 欣賞簡練文字，但覺得基調悲觀、結局灰暗；屬少數唱反調。

books.ken: What a person never says can shape a life as much as what they do.
books.kzh: 一個人從來唔講出口嘅嘢，對一生嘅影響可能同佢做過嘅事一樣大。

books.en: How Jeff Bezos turned an online bookshop into Amazon, a company that sells almost everything and runs much of the internet's cloud. A close look at his relentless focus on customers and long-term thinking.
books.zh: 貝佐斯點樣將一間網上書店，變成幾乎乜都賣、仲支撐住大半個互聯網雲端服務嘅 Amazon。書中仔細描寫佢對顧客嘅執著同長線思維。
books.ken: Start with what the customer needs and work backwards.
books.kzh: 由顧客需要出發，再倒推做法。

books.en: Astronaut Mark Watney is left behind on Mars, presumed dead. With limited food and a lot of ingenuity, he has to survive until rescue can reach him. Funny, tense and full of real science.
books.zh: 太空人 Mark Watney 被誤以為死咗，獨自留喺火星。糧食有限，佢要靠創意同科學知識生存到救援到達。故事搞笑、緊張，又充滿真實科學。
books.ken: Solve one problem, then the next, and keep going.
books.kzh: 解決一個問題，再解決下一個，咁就可以撐落去。

books.en: MIT physicist Max Tegmark asks what kind of future we want with artificial intelligence. He walks through possible worlds, from helpful AI to lost jobs to AI taking control, and argues we need to plan now.
books.zh: 麻省理工物理學家 Tegmark 問：我哋想同人工智能有一個點樣嘅未來？佢描繪咗唔同可能，由好幫手式嘅 AI、大量失業，到 AI 掌控世界，並認為而家就要開始計劃。
books.ken: The future of AI is not decided yet; it depends on choices we make now.
books.kzh: AI 嘅未來未有定案，取決於我哋而家嘅選擇。

books.prize_zh: 台北國際書展大獎 小說獎首獎
books.en: Hong Kong novelist Hon Lai-chu's first novel in about eight years is set in an emptied-out city after two waves of protest. Two art students meet in an oil-painting class, and the book follows their lives and those of an older generation shaped by the same upheavals. It cares less about plot than about bodies, relationships and what is left behind.
books.more_en: The structure is fragmented and layered, which reviewers read as fitting a city living with shared trauma. It is unsettling rather than comforting, but critics found real hope in its open spaces. One of three co-winners of the fiction prize at the 2026 Taipei International Book Exhibition Awards.
books.zh: 香港小說家韓麗珠相隔大約八年嘅長篇新作。故事發生喺兩場社會運動之後、人去樓空嘅城市。兩個喺油畫班相識嘅藝術學生，同埋上一代人，都被同一場巨變改寫咗人生。小說唔靠情節推進，而係專注寫身體、人與人嘅關係，同埋留低咗啲乜。
books.more_zh: 全書結構零碎、層層疊疊，評論認為正好配合一座城市集體創傷嘅狀態。睇落令人不安，但評論家喺佢嘅「空」入面見到希望。獲 2026 台北國際書展大獎小說獎首獎（三本並列之一）。

reviews.d: Hard to retell, he says; it is a direct stare at reality rather than a standard dystopia.
reviews.dz: 難以複述；唔係一般反烏托邦，而係直面現實。

reviews.d: The fragmented form suits collective trauma; ends with hope for open futures in the book's emptiness.
reviews.dz: 碎片式寫法切合集體創傷；喺空白之中見到未來嘅可能。

books.ken: After a city empties out, the people left behind still have to find a way to live and love.
books.kzh: 一座城清空之後，留低嘅人仍然要搵方法生活、去愛。

books.prize_zh: 台北國際書展大獎 小說獎首獎
books.en: A family returns home to a small town in central Taiwan, and that homecoming alternates with a present-day story set in the city. Lin Jun-ying, born in 1960 in Changhua, writes in a rich mix of Taiwanese, Mandarin, Japanese and English, full of allusions. The novel is a parable about land, language and identity under one regime after another.
books.more_en: It is demanding: twelve chapters and about 170,000 characters of dense prose that rewards slow reading. David Der-wei Wang's preface calls it a uniquely distinctive postmodern portrait. Not everyone agrees: one Taiwanese-language scholar finds its Taiwanese writing idiosyncratic and hard going. A co-winner of the 2026 Taipei Book Exhibition fiction prize.
books.zh: 一家人返到台灣中部小鎮嘅故鄉，呢段返鄉之旅同一條現代城市嘅故事線交替推進。1960 年生於彰化北斗嘅林俊頴，用台語、華語、日語同英語交織寫成，典故處處。小說係一則關於土地、語言同身份嘅寓言，寫台灣人喺一個又一個政權之下嘅命運。
books.more_zh: 呢本書要慢慢讀：12 章、大約十七萬字，文字密度好高。王德威喺推薦序稱佢係「相當獨特的小說」。亦有台語學者認為書中台語寫法太個人化、好難讀。獲 2026 台北國際書展大獎小說獎首獎（三本並列之一）。

reviews.src: 王德威 推薦序 (中國時報)
reviews.d: In his preface, Wang calls it unusually distinctive, a postmodern portrait braiding its two storylines.
reviews.dz: 推薦序：一部後現代畫像，兩條故事線交織，極之獨特。

reviews.d: A Taiwanese-language professor finds its Taiwanese writing idiosyncratic and hard to read; a dissenting view.
reviews.dz: 台語學者認為書中台語寫法難讀；屬唱反調嘅意見。

books.ken: Whoever controls the language of a place shapes how its people remember themselves.
books.kzh: 邊個掌握一個地方嘅語言，就影響住嗰度嘅人點樣記得自己。

books.t: The Origin of Species: Bebe Reborn
books.tz: 物種源始．貝貝重生：消失的可能世界
books.en: The final volume of Hong Kong writer Dung Kai-cheung's Natural History trilogy, about twenty years in the making. In V City, a place where reality and fiction blur, a theatre director, an actor and a mysterious writer work on a stage version of Kafka's 'A Hunger Artist'. A big, ambitious novel about making art and the worlds that might have been.
books.more_en: At about 270,000 characters it is a long read, and it reworks an older manuscript. In a 2026 interview with Taiwan's CNA, Dung said about 30,000 characters were drafted with the help of AI, which makes it an unusual experiment as well as the capstone of his work. The publisher's editor calls the book's history troubled.
books.zh: 香港作家董啟章「自然史三部曲」嘅最終卷，前後寫咗大約二十年。喺現實同虛構界線模糊嘅 V 城，一個劇場導演、一個演員同一個神秘作家，合力將卡夫卡《飢餓藝術家》搬上舞台。一部關於創作，同埋「消失咗嘅可能世界」嘅宏大小說。
books.more_zh: 全書大約二十七萬字，係改寫舊稿而成。董啟章 2026 年接受中央社訪問時透露，其中約三萬字係借助人工智能起稿，令呢本書除咗係佢創作生涯嘅總結，亦係一次特別嘅實驗。編者范銘如形容呢本書「命運多舛」。

reviews.d: The series editor's blurb frames it as the capstone of Dung's work, after a troubled history. (Publisher's note, not an independent review.)
reviews.dz: 編者推介：命運多舛，係作者創作嘅總結之作（出版社介紹）。

reviews.d: Interview: about 30,000 of its 270,000 characters were drafted with AI help, reworking an older manuscript.
reviews.dz: 訪問：二十七萬字中約三萬字由人工智能協助起稿。

books.ken: A novel can be a home for the worlds that never got the chance to exist.
books.kzh: 小說可以收留嗰啲從來冇機會出現嘅世界。

books.en: Most people think the world is getting worse, but the data says otherwise. Doctor and statistician Hans Rosling shows ten instincts that distort our view, and how to see the world more accurately.
books.zh: 大部份人以為世界越來越差，但數據話唔係。醫生兼統計學家羅斯林指出十種扭曲我哋睇法嘅本能，教你用事實更準確咁睇世界。
books.ken: Things can be bad and getting better at the same time.
books.kzh: 世界可以同時「仲係好差」同「越來越好」。

books.en: Classic essays on software projects by the manager of IBM's System/360. Its famous lesson: adding people to a late software project makes it later. Nearly fifty years on, it still explains why big projects slip.
books.zh: IBM System/360 項目經理寫嘅軟件工程經典。最有名嘅一課：一個已經遲咗嘅軟件項目，加人只會令佢更遲。近五十年後，仍然解釋到點解大型項目會延誤。
books.ken: Nine women cannot make a baby in one month.
books.kzh: 九個媽媽都唔可以一個月生個 BB 出嚟。

books.en: Richard Dawkins looks at evolution from the gene's point of view: bodies are vehicles that genes build to copy themselves. The book also coined the word "meme" for ideas that spread from mind to mind.
books.zh: 道金斯由基因嘅角度睇進化：身體只係基因為咗複製自己而建造嘅載具。呢本書亦創造咗「meme（迷因）」呢個字，形容喺人與人之間傳播嘅概念。
books.ken: Even kindness and cooperation can be explained by genes.
books.kzh: 就算係善良同合作，都可以用基因嚟解釋。

books.en: What computer science can teach us about everyday decisions: when to stop flat-hunting, how to organise a messy wardrobe, how to plan a busy day. A fun bridge between algorithms and ordinary life.
books.zh: 電腦科學可以點樣幫我哋做日常決定：幾時應該停止睇樓、點樣執一個亂糟糟嘅衣櫃、點樣安排忙碌嘅一日。將演算法同生活連埋一齊，好有趣。
books.ken: Look at the first 37% of options, then pick the next one that beats them all.
books.kzh: 先睇頭 37% 嘅選擇，之後揀第一個比佢哋全部好嘅。

books.en: Klara is a solar-powered robot companion who watches the world from a shop window, hoping to be chosen. A gentle, moving story by the Nobel prize winner about love, loneliness and what makes us human.
books.zh: Klara 係一個靠太陽能運作嘅機械人伴侶，每日喺店舖櫥窗觀察世界，期待被人揀中。諾貝爾文學獎得主石黑一雄用溫柔嘅筆觸，探討愛、孤獨同點樣先算係人。
books.ken: What makes a person special may live in the people who love them.
books.kzh: 一個人最獨特嘅地方，可能存在於愛佢嘅人心中。

books.en: PayPal co-founder Peter Thiel on building startups that create something truly new, rather than copying what already exists. He argues the best companies aim to become monopolies by being far better than anything else.
books.zh: PayPal 共同創辦人提爾講點樣創立真正創新嘅公司，而唔係抄襲現有嘅嘢。佢認為最好嘅公司，會因為遠遠勝過其他對手而成為壟斷者。
books.ken: What important truth do very few people agree with you on?
books.kzh: 有乜嘢重要嘅真理，係好少人同意你嘅？

books.en: Why did some societies conquer others? Jared Diamond argues it was not about people being smarter, but about geography: which plants and animals could be farmed, and how easily ideas spread across continents.
books.zh: 點解有啲社會征服咗其他社會？戴蒙認為原因唔係人比較聰明，而係地理：邊啲植物同動物可以馴化，以及知識喺各大洲之間有幾容易傳播。
books.ken: Geography, not people, shaped which civilisations grew powerful.
books.kzh: 決定文明強弱嘅，係地理環境，而唔係人種。

books.en: The true story of Theranos, a Silicon Valley start-up that claimed it could run hundreds of tests from a drop of blood. A Wall Street Journal reporter reveals how the technology never worked and how the secret came out.
books.zh: 矽谷初創 Theranos 嘅真實故事：佢聲稱一滴血就可以做幾百項檢測。《華爾街日報》記者揭露呢項技術根本從未成功，以及真相點樣被揭發。
books.ken: A great story is no substitute for technology that actually works.
books.kzh: 故事講得幾動聽，都代替唔到真正行得通嘅技術。

books.en: In a world of constant surveillance ruled by Big Brother, Winston Smith quietly begins to question the Party. Orwell's classic gave us words like "Big Brother" and "thoughtcrime" and is still widely read today.
books.zh: 喺一個由「老大哥」統治、無時無刻被監視嘅世界，Winston Smith 開始暗中質疑黨。奧威爾嘅經典為我哋留低「老大哥」、「思想罪」等詞語，至今仍然廣為傳閱。
books.ken: Whoever controls the past controls the future.
books.kzh: 誰控制過去，就控制未來。

books.en: Kai-Fu Lee, who worked at Apple, Microsoft and Google, compares how China and the US are racing in artificial intelligence, and what AI will mean for jobs. He ends with a personal story about what machines cannot replace.
books.zh: 曾任職蘋果、微軟同 Google 嘅李開復，比較中美兩國點樣喺人工智能領域競爭，以及 AI 對工作嘅影響。結尾分享佢嘅個人經歷，講機器取代唔到嘅嘢。
books.ken: As AI takes over routine work, human care and love become more valuable.
books.kzh: 當 AI 接手重複性工作，人與人之間嘅關懷就更加珍貴。

books.en: A pilot stranded in the desert meets a little prince from a tiny planet. A short, beautifully illustrated story for children and adults about friendship, love and seeing what really matters.
books.zh: 一位飛機師喺沙漠迫降，遇到嚟自一個細小星球嘅小王子。一本插圖優美嘅短篇故事，啱晒大人細路一齊睇，講友誼、愛，同埋看見真正重要嘅嘢。
books.ken: What is essential is invisible to the eye.
books.kzh: 真正重要嘅嘢，用眼係睇唔到嘅。

books.t: Hackers: Heroes of the Computer Revolution
books.en: The original hackers were not criminals but curious tinkerers. Levy tells the stories of MIT students, Silicon Valley hobbyists and young game makers who shaped personal computing, and the "hacker ethic" of sharing and openness.
books.zh: 最早嘅「黑客」唔係罪犯，而係好奇心爆燈嘅發燒友。作者講述麻省理工學生、矽谷電腦愛好者同年輕遊戲製作人點樣塑造個人電腦，以及佢哋分享、開放嘅「黑客精神」。
books.ken: Information wants to be free, and hands-on curiosity drives progress.
books.kzh: 資訊應該自由流通，動手嘅好奇心推動進步。

books.en: Computer science professor Cal Newport argues that the ability to focus without distraction is becoming rare and valuable. He gives practical rules for cutting back on email and social media to do your best work.
books.zh: 電腦科學教授 Newport 認為，唔受干擾、全神貫注嘅能力越嚟越罕有，亦越嚟越有價值。佢提供實用方法，減少電郵同社交媒體，專心做出最好嘅成果。
books.ken: Long blocks of focused time beat a day full of small interruptions.
books.kzh: 一大段專注時間，勝過被打斷無數次嘅一整日。

books.en: A former Wall Street data scientist shows how computer models that decide loans, jobs and prison sentences can be unfair, secret and hard to challenge, and how they can quietly make inequality worse.
books.zh: 前華爾街數據科學家揭示，決定貸款、求職同刑期嘅電腦模型，可以好唔公平、唔透明又難以挑戰，仲會靜靜雞令貧富不均更嚴重。
books.ken: An algorithm is an opinion written in code.
books.kzh: 演算法其實係用程式寫出嚟嘅主觀意見。

books.en: Nike's founder tells how he started by selling Japanese running shoes from the boot of his car. An honest memoir about near bankruptcy, loyal friends and the crazy risks behind building a global brand.
books.zh: Nike 創辦人講述自己點樣由車尾箱賣日本跑鞋起家。一本坦誠嘅回憶錄，講瀕臨破產、忠心嘅夥伴，以及建立全球品牌背後嘅瘋狂冒險。
books.ken: Don't stop. Keep going even when the finish line is not in sight.
books.kzh: 唔好停，就算睇唔到終點都要繼續行。

books.en: The story of Bell Labs, where the transistor, the laser, solar cells and information theory were invented. Gertner explains how one research lab, full of brilliant people sharing long corridors, shaped the modern world.
books.zh: 貝爾實驗室嘅故事：電晶體、激光、太陽能電池同資訊理論都喺呢度誕生。作者解釋點解一間充滿天才、走廊長長嘅研究所，可以塑造現代世界。
books.ken: Put clever people from different fields together and let them talk.
books.kzh: 將唔同範疇嘅聰明人放埋一齊，等佢哋多啲傾偈。

books.tz: 基因：人類最親密的歷史
books.en: A doctor's history of the gene, from Mendel's pea plants to DNA and gene editing, woven with his own family's history of mental illness. It asks what we should do now that we can read and rewrite our genes.
books.zh: 一位醫生寫嘅基因史：由孟德爾嘅豌豆實驗，到 DNA 同基因編輯，並穿插佢家族嘅精神病史。書中追問：而家我哋可以閱讀同改寫基因，應該點做？
books.ken: Genes shape us, but they are not the whole story of who we are.
books.kzh: 基因塑造我哋，但唔係我哋嘅全部。

books.en: The story of Jennifer Doudna and the discovery of CRISPR, a tool that can edit DNA like a word processor edits text. It covers the race to the Nobel Prize, COVID vaccines and the hard questions about editing humans.
books.zh: 講述 Jennifer Doudna 同 CRISPR 嘅發現：一種可以好似文書處理咁編輯 DNA 嘅工具。書中包括爭奪諾貝爾獎嘅競賽、新冠疫苗，以及編輯人類基因帶來嘅倫理難題。
books.ken: We can now rewrite life's code; deciding when we should is the hard part.
books.kzh: 我哋已經可以改寫生命密碼，難在決定幾時應該咁做。

books.en: Nineteen short stories about how people really behave with money. Housel argues that doing well with money is less about knowing finance and more about patience, humility and not wanting too much.
books.zh: 十九個短篇故事，講人喺金錢面前嘅真實行為。作者認為理財成功唔係靠識幾多金融知識，而係靠耐性、謙虛同唔貪心。
books.ken: Enough is a number; know yours.
books.kzh: 「夠」係一個數字，要知道你嘅係幾多。

books.t: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
books.tz: 仿生人會夢見電子羊嗎？
books.en: In a ruined future San Francisco, bounty hunter Rick Deckard hunts androids who look exactly like people. The novel behind the film Blade Runner asks what separates humans from machines: maybe empathy.
books.zh: 喺殘破嘅未來三藩市，賞金獵人 Rick Deckard 追捕外表同人一模一樣嘅仿生人。電影 Blade Runner 嘅原著小說，追問人同機器嘅分別，可能就係同理心。
books.ken: Empathy may be what truly makes us human.
books.kzh: 同理心，可能先係令我哋成為人嘅關鍵。

books.en: How do you teach a machine to do what we actually want, not just what we said? Christian tells the stories of researchers wrestling with biased data, tricky rewards and AI that finds loopholes, in clear and human language.
books.zh: 點樣教機器做我哋真正想要嘅嘢，而唔係只係照字面做？作者用清楚易明嘅文字，講研究人員點樣處理有偏見嘅數據、難搞嘅獎勵機制，同識得「走漏洞」嘅 AI。
books.ken: A system does exactly what you reward, not what you meant.
books.kzh: 系統只會做你獎勵佢做嘅嘢，而唔係你心目中想佢做嘅嘢。

books.en: Having largely beaten famine, plague and war, what will humans aim for next? Harari imagines a future of longer lives, upgraded bodies and powerful algorithms, and asks what happens when data knows us better than we know ourselves.
books.zh: 人類大致戰勝咗饑荒、瘟疫同戰爭之後，下一個目標係乜？哈拉瑞想像一個長壽、身體升級同演算法當道嘅未來，並問：當數據比我哋更了解自己，會點？
books.ken: Whoever owns the data may hold the power.
books.kzh: 誰擁有數據，誰就可能掌握權力。

books.en: Why can't we work out which way a door opens, or how to use a new remote? Former Apple designer Don Norman explains that bad design, not the user, is usually to blame, and how good design guides us without instructions.
books.zh: 點解我哋成日唔知道門應該推定拉，又唔識用新遙控？前蘋果設計師 Norman 解釋，問題通常出喺設計差，而唔係用家，以及好設計點樣唔使說明書都令人識用。
books.ken: If people keep making the same mistake, fix the design, not the people.
books.kzh: 如果大家成日犯同一個錯，要改嘅係設計，唔係人。

books.en: A washed-up hacker gets one last job in a neon-lit future of cyberspace, powerful corporations and artificial intelligence. The book that defined cyberpunk and popularised the word "cyberspace", years before the web existed.
books.zh: 一個落泊嘅黑客，喺一個霓虹閃爍、充滿網絡空間、大企業同人工智能嘅未來，接下最後一單任務。呢本書定義咗「賽博朋克」，仲喺互聯網普及之前已經令「cyberspace」一詞流行。
books.ken: Science fiction often names the future before it arrives.
books.kzh: 科幻小說往往喺未來到嚟之前，就幫佢改好名。

books.en: Why do great, well-run companies fail? Harvard professor Clayton Christensen shows how cheaper, simpler "disruptive" technologies sneak up from below while leaders keep listening to their best customers.
books.zh: 點解管理得好好嘅大公司都會失敗？哈佛教授 Christensen 指出，更平、更簡單嘅「破壞性創新」會由低端悄悄冒起，而龍頭企業仍然只顧聽最好嘅客戶意見。
books.ken: Doing everything right can still make you miss the next big thing.
books.kzh: 樣樣做啱，都有可能錯過下一個大潮流。

books.en: Neuroscientist Matthew Walker explains what sleep does for memory, mood, health and creativity, and why so many of us do not get enough. A persuasive case for treating sleep as seriously as diet and exercise.
books.zh: 神經科學家 Walker 解釋睡眠對記憶、情緒、健康同創意嘅作用，以及點解咁多人瞓唔夠。佢有力咁說服你：睡眠同飲食、運動一樣重要。
books.ken: Sleep is not lost time; it is when the brain does its maintenance.
books.kzh: 瞓覺唔係浪費時間，而係大腦做保養嘅時候。

books.en: Why do so many predictions fail, from the weather to elections to the economy? Statistician Nate Silver explains how to find the real signal in noisy data and why thinking in probabilities makes better forecasts.
books.zh: 點解咁多預測都失準？由天氣、選舉到經濟都係。統計學家 Silver 講解點樣喺雜亂數據中搵出真正訊號，以及用機率思考點樣令預測更準。
books.ken: Good forecasters think in probabilities and update as new facts arrive.
books.kzh: 好嘅預測者用機率思考，有新資料就即刻修正。

books.t: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
books.en: Seconds before Earth is demolished for a space bypass, Arthur Dent is rescued by his friend Ford, who turns out to be an alien. A wildly funny space adventure, and the reason geeks everywhere know the answer is 42.
books.zh: 地球為咗起太空快速公路而被拆毀前一刻，Arthur Dent 被好友 Ford 救走，原來 Ford 係外星人。一個超級搞笑嘅太空冒險，亦係點解全世界嘅科技迷都知道答案係 42。
books.ken: Don't panic, and always know where your towel is.
books.kzh: 唔好驚，記住帶埋條毛巾。

books.en: A biography of the entrepreneur behind Tesla and SpaceX, from a tough childhood in South Africa to rockets that land themselves. Vance shows both the huge ambition and the punishing way Musk drives his teams.
books.zh: Tesla 同 SpaceX 背後企業家嘅傳記，由佢喺南非艱苦嘅童年，講到可以自己降落嘅火箭。作者同時描寫佢巨大嘅野心，以及對團隊近乎嚴苛嘅要求。
books.ken: Aim at problems so big that most people think they are impossible.
books.kzh: 瞄準大部份人都覺得冇可能解決嘅大問題。

books.en: Why do some people succeed far beyond others? Gladwell argues that talent is only part of the story: birth dates, culture, lucky timing and around 10,000 hours of practice matter just as much.
books.zh: 點解有啲人特別成功？葛拉威爾認為天份只係其中一部份：出生日期、文化背景、時機，以及大約一萬個鐘嘅練習，同樣重要。
books.ken: Success is built on opportunity and practice, not talent alone.
books.kzh: 成功靠機遇同練習，唔只係天份。

books.en: Harvard professor Shoshana Zuboff explains how tech companies turn our clicks, locations and habits into data that predicts and nudges what we do next, and why that is a new kind of power.
books.zh: 哈佛教授 Zuboff 解釋科技公司點樣將我哋嘅點擊、位置同習慣變成數據，用嚟預測甚至引導我哋下一步嘅行為，以及點解呢個係一種新形式嘅權力。
books.ken: If a service is free, your behaviour may be the product.
books.kzh: 如果服務係免費，你嘅行為可能就係產品。

books.en: Mathematician Hari Seldon predicts the fall of the Galactic Empire and a dark age of 30,000 years. His plan: set up a Foundation to shorten it. A classic of science fiction about history, science and power.
books.zh: 數學家謝頓預測銀河帝國即將崩潰，之後會有三萬年黑暗時代。佢嘅計劃係成立「基地」去縮短呢段時期。一部講歷史、科學同權力嘅科幻經典。
books.ken: You cannot predict one person, but you can predict crowds.
books.kzh: 一個人難以預測，但一大群人嘅行為可以。

books.en: Pixar co-founder Ed Catmull shares how the studio behind Toy Story keeps creativity alive: honest feedback sessions, embracing early ugly drafts, and protecting new ideas while they are still fragile.
books.zh: Pixar 共同創辦人 Catmull 分享《反斗奇兵》背後嘅工作室點樣保持創意：坦白直接嘅意見交流、接受最初嘅「醜陋」草稿，以及保護仲好脆弱嘅新點子。
books.ken: Early ideas are ugly babies; protect them while they grow.
books.kzh: 新點子初時都好「醜」，要保護佢慢慢成長。

books.en: Jin Yong's best-loved martial arts novel, first published in a Hong Kong newspaper. Guo Jing, a slow but honest young man raised on the Mongolian steppe, becomes a great hero through loyalty, hard work and his clever friend Huang Rong.
books.zh: 金庸最受歡迎嘅武俠小說，最初喺香港報章連載。喺蒙古草原長大、資質平平但為人正直嘅郭靖，憑住忠義、苦練同聰明伶俐嘅黃蓉，成為一代大俠。
books.ken: Steady effort and a good heart can beat raw talent.
books.kzh: 勤力同善良，可以勝過天份。

books.en: The story of John Carmack and John Romero, two young programmers whose games Wolfenstein 3D, Doom and Quake created the first-person shooter and changed video games forever. A tale of genius, friendship and falling out.
books.zh: 講 John Carmack 同 John Romero 兩位年輕程式員嘅故事：佢哋製作嘅《德軍總部 3D》、《Doom》同《Quake》開創咗第一身射擊遊戲，永遠改變咗電子遊戲。一個關於天才、友誼同決裂嘅故事。
books.ken: Small teams with a clear vision can change a whole industry.
books.kzh: 目標清晰嘅細團隊，都可以改變整個行業。

books.tz: 垃圾場長大的自學人生
books.en: Tara Westover grew up in rural Idaho with parents who did not believe in school or hospitals. She first stepped into a classroom at 17, and went on to earn a PhD from Cambridge. A powerful memoir about family and self-invention.
books.zh: Tara Westover 喺美國愛達荷州鄉郊長大，父母唔信學校亦唔信醫院。佢 17 歲先第一次踏入課室，最後喺劍橋大學攞到博士。一本關於家庭同重塑自我嘅震撼回憶錄。
books.ken: Education can give you the power to see your own life differently.
books.kzh: 教育令你有能力用另一個角度睇自己嘅人生。

books.en: How the internet began: the story of ARPANET in the 1960s and 70s, and the engineers who worked out how to make distant computers talk to each other, inventing email and the rules that still run the internet today.
books.zh: 互聯網點樣誕生：講述 1960 至 70 年代嘅 ARPANET，以及一班工程師點樣令相隔好遠嘅電腦互相溝通，順帶發明咗電郵，同今日仍然支撐住互聯網嘅規則。
books.ken: The internet was designed to keep working even when parts of it break.
books.kzh: 互聯網嘅設計，係就算部份壞咗都照樣運作。

books.en: A divorced woman from Shanghai and a wealthy playboy play a careful game of romance in Hong Kong, until the Japanese invasion in 1941 changes everything. Eileen Chang's sharp, elegant story is set around Repulse Bay.
books.zh: 一個離咗婚嘅上海女子，同一個富家公子喺香港展開一場步步為營嘅愛情角力，直至 1941 年日軍攻港，一切都改變。張愛玲以淺水灣為背景，寫得尖銳又優雅。
books.ken: Sometimes it takes a whole city falling for two people to find each other.
books.kzh: 有時要成座城淪陷，兩個人先真正走埋一齊。

books.en: Mathematician Hannah Fry looks at algorithms already making decisions about us, in hospitals, courts, cars and shopping. Lively and balanced, she asks when we should trust machines and when humans must stay in charge.
books.zh: 數學家 Hannah Fry 探討已經喺醫院、法庭、汽車同購物中替我哋做決定嘅演算法。佢寫得生動又持平，問我哋幾時應該信機器，幾時一定要由人話事。
books.ken: The best results often come from humans and machines working together.
books.kzh: 最好嘅結果，往往來自人同機器合作。

books.en: Should you specialise early or try many things? David Epstein argues that in a complex world, generalists who sample widely and start late often do better, connecting ideas that specialists miss.
books.zh: 應該早早專注一樣嘢，定係多方面嘗試？作者認為喺複雜嘅世界，涉獵廣泛、起步較遲嘅「通才」往往更出色，因為佢哋可以連結專家睇唔到嘅意念。
books.ken: A broad mix of experiences helps you solve new kinds of problems.
books.kzh: 經歷越廣，越識得解決新類型嘅問題。

books.en: An astronomer working as a systems manager notices a 75-cent accounting error, and follows it to a hacker selling secrets to the KGB. A true detective story from the early days of computer security, still gripping today.
books.zh: 一位兼職做系統管理員嘅天文學家，發現帳目差咗 75 仙，一路追查，竟然揪出一個將機密賣俾蘇聯 KGB 嘅黑客。電腦保安初期嘅真實偵探故事，到今日睇仍然好緊張。
books.ken: Small oddities are worth chasing; they can uncover big problems.
books.kzh: 細微嘅異常值得追查，可能揭發大問題。

books.en: Linked short stories about robots that follow the Three Laws of Robotics, and the surprising ways those simple rules go wrong. Written in the 1940s, they still shape how we talk about safe AI.
books.zh: 一系列互相關連嘅短篇故事，講遵守「機械人三定律」嘅機械人，以及呢幾條簡單規則點樣出人意表咁出錯。寫於 1940 年代，至今仍影響我哋點樣討論 AI 安全。
books.ken: Even simple rules can have unexpected results.
books.kzh: 再簡單嘅規則，都可能帶嚟意想不到嘅後果。

books.en: DeepMind co-founder Mustafa Suleyman warns that AI and synthetic biology are spreading faster than any technology before. He explains why they will be hard to contain and what governments and companies could do.
books.zh: DeepMind 共同創辦人 Suleyman 警告，人工智能同合成生物學嘅擴散速度前所未見。佢解釋點解呢啲技術好難受控，以及政府同企業可以做啲乜。
books.ken: Powerful technology tends to spread; containing it takes deliberate effort.
books.kzh: 強大嘅技術總會擴散，要控制佢就要刻意努力。

books.t: The Old Man and the Sea
books.en: An old Cuban fisherman who has gone 84 days without a catch hooks a giant marlin far out at sea. A short, simple and powerful story about courage, pride and never giving up.
books.zh: 一個連續 84 日都捉唔到魚嘅古巴老漁夫，喺遠海釣到一條巨大嘅馬林魚。一個簡短、樸實但好有力量嘅故事，講勇氣、尊嚴同永不放棄。
books.ken: A man can be destroyed but not defeated.
books.kzh: 人可以被毀滅，但唔可以被打敗。

books.t: The Hard Thing About Hard Things
books.tz: 什麼才是經營最難的事？
books.en: Silicon Valley investor Ben Horowitz shares the brutal, honest truth about running a tech company when things go wrong: layoffs, near-bankruptcy and making decisions with no good options.
books.zh: 矽谷投資者 Horowitz 坦白分享經營科技公司遇上困境時嘅殘酷真相：裁員、瀕臨破產，以及喺冇好選擇之下都要做決定。
books.ken: There is no recipe for hard problems; you have to face them head-on.
books.kzh: 難題冇公式，只能夠正面迎戰。

books.en: A Wired journalist tracks a group of state hackers who switched off power in Ukraine and released NotPetya, the most costly cyberattack in history. A thriller-like look at how cyberwar reaches everyday life.
books.zh: 《Wired》記者追蹤一個國家級黑客組織：佢哋令烏克蘭停電，仲放出史上損失最大嘅網絡攻擊 NotPetya。好似驚悚小說咁，講網絡戰點樣影響日常生活。
books.ken: In a connected world, a cyberattack can spread far beyond its target.
books.kzh: 喺互聯世界，網絡攻擊可以波及目標以外好遠嘅地方。

books.tz_note: 未有中譯 No Chinese edition yet
books.prize_zh: 金匠獎 2026（獎勵突破常規嘅英國小說）
books.en: China Miéville's huge new novel, about 1,200 pages long, won the 2026 Goldsmiths Prize, the British award for fiction that "breaks the mould" and stretches what a novel can do. Miéville is best known for strange, richly built worlds such as Perdido Street Station and The City & the City.
books.zh: 英國作家 China Miéville 嘅新長篇，厚達約 1,200 頁，奪得 2026 金匠獎。呢個獎專門頒畀「打破常規」、挑戰小說形式嘅作品。Miéville 以構建奇異世界見稱，代表作有《帕迪多街車站》、《被謀殺的城市》。

books.tz_note: 未有中譯 No Chinese edition yet
books.prize: Walter Scott Prize for Historical Fiction 2026
books.prize_zh: 華特·司各特歷史小說獎 2026
books.en: A historical novel that follows the life of a girl who cannot speak, growing up in Austria under the Nazis. It won the 2026 Walter Scott Prize, the UK's main award for historical fiction, ahead of a shortlist that included Graeme Macrae Burnet and Benjamin Wood.
books.zh: 歷史小說，寫一個唔識講嘢嘅女仔，喺納粹統治下嘅奧地利成長嘅一生。奪得 2026 年華特·司各特歷史小說獎，係英國最重要嘅歷史小說獎項。

books.prize: Taiwan Literature Award 2026, Book of the Year
books.prize_zh: 2026 臺灣文學獎金典獎 年度大獎
books.en: Liu Tzu-chieh's first story collection in twelve years: nine stories about death, and how it seeps into ordinary days. One of them, set in Atami with a ghost, had already won the 2025 Yeh Shih-tao short story prize. Liu is best known for Seven Days in Heaven, about a family funeral.
books.zh: 劉梓潔相隔十二年嘅短篇小說集，九個故事都係寫死亡，同埋死亡點樣滲入日常生活。其中〈再生，涼子，以及與幽靈共度的熱海〉早已攞過 2025 葉石濤短篇小說獎首獎。佢最出名嘅作品係寫家人喪禮嘅《父後七日》。奪得 2026 臺灣文學獎金典獎年度大獎。

books.prize_zh: 2026 金鼎獎 文學圖書獎
books.en: A novel grown out of the author's years of walking Taiwan's mountains. Two story lines run side by side, weaving together the colonial past, Indigenous and Japanese history, and the struggle between people and nature in the forests. It won a 2026 Golden Tripod Award for literature, alongside Naked Mountain and Lightning in July.
books.zh: 作者多年行山踏查台灣山林寫成嘅小說，用雙線敘事，將殖民歷史、原住民同日本人嘅過去，同埋人與自然之間嘅角力織埋一齊。獲 2026 金鼎獎文學圖書獎，同《裸山》、《七月爍爁》同屆得獎。
